findings.summary: The caption's first sentence is an administrative series label rather than a hook, burying the actual hook in sentence two.
findings.evidence: "Part 3 of DOCKER IMAGES: LAYERS, CACHE, LEAN BUILDS. Your 1.1GB Node image and your cache miss on every single push are the same bug: ..."
findings.fix: Lead with the hook and demote the label: "Your 1.1GB Node image and your cache miss on every single push are the same bug: you put the thing that changes most at the bottom of the stack. (Part 3 of DOCKER IMAGES: LAYERS, CACHE, LEAN BUILDS.)"

findings.summary: The base-image decision rule and the "compare on four axes" wrap-up appear on page 1, before the comparison table and the musl/glibc explanation that justify them on page 2.
findings.evidence: Page 1 opens with "7. Picking One" → "Static compiled binary → scratch or distroless-static", "JVM, Node, Python needing glibc → distroless-* or slim" and the callout "Compare On Four Axes … Size, build time, CVE surface, debuggability"; the defining material — the table rows "alpine | musl | busybox sh | ~7MB" … "scratch | none | none | 0MB" and "Alpine ships ==musl==, so glibc-only manylinux wheels never match" — only arrives on page 2.
findings.fix: Move the "7. Picking One" qa block and the "Compare On Four Axes" callout out of page 1 and place them on page 2 immediately after "Scratch Needs Certs", so the cheat-sheet table, the alpine trap paragraph and the scratch/certs code come first and the decision rule closes the chapter.

findings.summary: `adduser --system app` does not create a group named `app`, so the `COPY --chown=app:app` advised on the same page fails — and the flag doesn't exist at all on Alpine's busybox adduser.
findings.evidence: "RUN adduser --system app" paired with "Own the app dir at copy time: `COPY --chown=app:app`"
findings.fix: Use `RUN adduser --system --group app` on Debian/slim (adduser(8): system users get `nogroup` as primary group unless `--group` is passed), and show the busybox form `RUN adduser -S -D -H app` for the alpine bases used elsewhere in this part — `--system` errors with "unrecognized option" there.

findings.summary: The Alpine Trap claim that pip always compiles C extensions from source on musl is outdated — musllinux wheels (PEP 656) are published for most mainstream C-extension packages.
findings.evidence: "Alpine ships ==musl==, so glibc-only manylinux wheels never match and pip compiles C extensions from source. Builds run **5-10x** slower"
findings.fix: Reword to: manylinux wheels never match, so pip needs a `musllinux` wheel; numpy, pandas, cryptography, pydantic and friends now ship them, but anything without a musllinux wheel still builds from source — that tail is where the 5-10x hit and the gcc-bloated image come from.

findings.summary: The decorative pushpin graphic sits on top of the closing braces of the Go template in the "Verify Before You Push" code block, obscuring syntax-critical characters.
findings.evidence: docker image inspect img \ --format '{{.Config.User}}' — the pin head covers the final "}}'" glyphs at the end of the line.
findings.fix: Move the pushpin anchor for the "empty User field means root" sticky note down and left so it attaches to the note's top edge without crossing the code line above it.

findings.summary: The numbered anti-pattern run 1–6 is broken apart by the base-image chapter and then collides with a second series restarting at 1 on the same page.
findings.evidence: Page 1 runs "1. The Big Five" → "4. Pin And Refresh"; page 2 has "5. Never Ship As Root" followed by "Base Image Cheat Sheet" / "The Alpine Trap" / "Scratch Needs Certs"; page 3 then opens with "6. Surface And Churn" and immediately restarts at "1. Node: Build Stage".
findings.fix: Keep the anti-pattern series contiguous: move "6. Surface And Churn" up to directly follow "5. Never Ship As Root" on page 2 and relocate the base-image blocks (cheat sheet, alpine trap, scratch certs) to page 1 in place of the ch-7 blocks moved there, so page 3 contains only the recipe series 1–5.

findings.summary: The Python recipe shows only the builder stage, so the venv it creates is never copied or put on PATH and the example cannot be used as written.
findings.evidence: "4. Python: slim + venv" ends at "RUN /opt/venv/bin/pip install \ --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt" — there is no runtime stage and no `ENV PATH=/opt/venv/bin:$PATH`, unlike the Node recipe which gets both "1. Node: Build Stage" and "2. Node: Runtime Stage".
findings.fix: Add a second Python code block ("5. Python: Runtime Stage") with `FROM python:3.12-slim` / `COPY --from=build /opt/venv /opt/venv` / `ENV PATH=/opt/venv/bin:$PATH` / exec-form CMD, and renumber the Go recipe accordingly.

findings.summary: The hashtag #kubernetes is off-topic for a carousel that covers only image build mechanics, with no orchestration content anywhere in the part.
findings.evidence: "#kubernetes" in the hashtag list, while the part's pages cover only anti-patterns, BuildKit secrets, digest pinning, non-root users, base images, and Node/Python/Go Dockerfile recipes.
findings.fix: Replace "#kubernetes" with a build-relevant tag such as "#distroless" or "#containersecurity".

findings.summary: Pushpin graphics overlap code glyphs in two dashed code blocks, partially covering characters.
findings.evidence: && echo "$SHA f.tgz" | sha256sum -c (pin sits between "sha256" and "sum") and FROM node@sha256:9f0c... # ✓ frozen (pin covers the "✓").
findings.fix: Offset both pushpins so they sit within the yellow sticky notes' top margin rather than over the preceding code line, or add ~12px of bottom padding to the code blocks so the pin lands in whitespace.

findings.summary: The `ADD --checksum` example gates itself on a Dockerfile syntax version the handbook never introduces.
findings.evidence: "# syntax < 1.6 → curl + verify:" in the "3. Downloads With Proof" code block — no `# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1.x` directive or frontend-version concept appears anywhere in the part.
findings.fix: Add a one-line note defining the directive (e.g. `# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1.6` at the top of the Dockerfile selects the BuildKit frontend) before using "syntax < 1.6" as a condition, or restate the fallback as "older BuildKit → curl + verify".

findings.summary: Page 1's title omits the base-image-selection material that opens the page, so the first two blocks a reader sees are not covered by the title.
findings.evidence: Title "Anti-Patterns, Secrets & Digest Pinning" vs. the page's opening blocks: heading "7. Picking One", Q&A "Why does `docker exec -it app sh` fail on my distroless image?", and callout "Compare On Four Axes" ("Size, build time, CVE surface, debuggability").
findings.fix: Either retitle page 1 to cover the lead-in (e.g. "Picking a Base, Anti-Patterns & Digest Pinning") or move the "7. Picking One" Q&A and "Compare On Four Axes" callout onto page 2, whose title already claims "Choosing a Base Image".

findings.summary: TCP fallback is listed as a live Alpine DNS problem, but musl gained DNS TCP fallback in 1.2.4, shipped in Alpine 3.18 (2023).
findings.fix: Drop TCP fallback or qualify it as "pre-3.18 only"; keep the still-valid resolver gaps (no `options ndots`, all nameservers queried in parallel, search-domain handling).

findings.summary: The cheat sheet lists distroless as glibc, but distroless/static — the ~2MB end of its own size range and the Go base recommended on page 3 — contains no libc at all.
findings.fix: Split the row: `distroless/static` → libc "none", ~2MB; `distroless/base` and the language variants → glibc, ~20-50MB.

findings.summary: `docker history` truncates the CREATED BY column by default, so the callout overstates what a plain invocation reveals.
findings.evidence: "`docker history ` prints every build arg and command."
findings.fix: Write `docker history --no-trunc ` — the default output cuts the command off and can hide the very `|1 TOKEN=… /bin/sh -c …` prefix you are looking for.

findings.summary: The verification command `docker run --rm img id` cannot run on the scratch and distroless images this page recommends, since neither ships an `id` binary.
findings.fix: Note that `id` only exists on alpine/slim; for scratch and distroless rely on `docker image inspect --format '{{.Config.User}}'` (already shown) or `docker run --rm --entrypoint sh img:debug -c id`.

findings.summary: `BUILDKIT_INLINE_CACHE=1` is offered as the cache-sharing answer for builds that are all multi-stage, but inline cache only exports final-image layers and cannot restore builder-stage layers.
findings.evidence: "`BUILDKIT_INLINE_CACHE=1` ships cache metadata" alongside the multi-stage Node/Python/Go recipes
findings.fix: Add that inline cache is min-mode only and doesn't cover intermediate stages; for multi-stage use `--cache-to=type=registry,ref=…,mode=max --cache-from=type=registry,ref=…`.

findings.summary: The LABEL line references `$REPO` without a preceding `ARG REPO`, so it silently produces an empty label rather than the source URL.
findings.fix: Add `ARG REPO` (per stage) above the LABEL, or hardcode the URL; an undeclared variable expands to the empty string and the provenance label ships blank.

findings.summary: The reason exec-form CMD matters is given two blocks after the example that silently relies on it, filed under the Go recipe where it does not belong.
findings.evidence: "3. Ship It Safely" asserts only `CMD ["node","dist/main.js"]  # exec form`, while the supporting reason — "Shell-form CMD wraps in `/bin/sh -c` and swallows SIGTERM" — is the last bullet of "5. Go Recipe".
findings.fix: Move the SIGTERM bullet into "3. Ship It Safely" next to the exec-form CMD line, since it is a general rule rather than a Go-specific one.

findings.summary: The LABEL example interpolates a build variable that is never declared, so the label would be empty as written.
findings.evidence: "LABEL org.opencontainers.image.source=$REPO" in "3. Ship It Safely", with no `ARG REPO` anywhere in the recipe.
findings.fix: Either add `ARG REPO` immediately above the LABEL line, or hardcode the value (`LABEL org.opencontainers.image.source=https://github.com/org/app`).
